subject: Post-demo technical follow-up: SDK auth, routing, and prompt stewardship
messages:
From: Jamie Torres <jamie.torres@edgewave.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@edgewave.ai
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Thanks for the demo — a few technical clarifications

Vivek,

Thanks for the walkthrough today — the latency numbers and the dedicated routing options looked promising. A few quick technical follow-ups from our engineering team so we can scope an internal POC: 

- SDKs: Does Redwood provide official client SDKs for Typescript and Python? We prefer a minimal install footprint (no native builds) for our serverless workers. Any sample repos or quickstart snippets you can share would help speed our eval.

- Auth: We need to understand supported auth patterns. Our security lead prefers short-lived mTLS creds if possible, but API keys scoped by workload are acceptable for an initial POC. Do you support OAuth + service tokens or only bearer keys? Any examples of rotation/CI integration would be great.

- Routing & multi-region: We have users in both NA and EU. Can requests be pinned by region or routed automatically to the nearest compatible model? How do fallbacks behave when a model variant is unavailable?

- Structured output / tool calling: We liked the tool-calling demo — can we request deterministic structured JSON for downstream orchestration (e.g., {"action":"invoke_agent","args":{...}})? Any best-practice for schema evolution / versioning?

- Embeddings / rerankers: For our relevance layer, we'd like a recommended config for embedding dimensionality, index cadence, and a reranker approach (embedding-only vs. hybrid with a lightweight cross-encoder).

- Prompt governance: We need an outline of how Redwood recommends versioning system prompts, defending against prompt injection, and running red-team tests prior to production rollout. Is that something you help scope with customers?

If you can share an integration checklist and propose a 45-min technical follow-up this week (with an engineer), we can try to get procurement looped in next week.

Cheers,
Jamie Torres
Head of Product
EdgeWave AI

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Torres <jamie.torres@edgewave.ai>
Cc: procurement@edgewave.ai, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 17:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — a few technical clarifications

Jamie — thanks, really helpful questions. Quick answers inline and then a proposed next step: a technical deep-dive with Grace (solutions) + Hiro (runtime eng) to go through architecture and a short PoC checklist.

- SDKs: We publish official TS and Python SDKs (pure JS build for TS/Node; wheel for Python). I attached a short integration checklist that points to the sample repos and a tiny sandbox snippet for serverless use.

- Auth: We support bearer API keys out of the box, OAuth 2.0 client credentials for long-lived service accounts, and optional mTLS for private deployments. We can demonstrate token rotation patterns with HashiCorp Vault or built-in KMS integration.

- Routing/multi-region: Routing policy is pluggable — you can pin by region or use latency/cost policy with automatic fallback to a compatible model family. Fallbacks will route to the nearest model variant that matches capability constraints; we also support a configurable "graceful degradation" policy (e.g., fallback to lower-precision quantized model before queuing).

- Structured output / tool calling: The runtime can return constrained JSON via a schema contract and we support explicit tool-calling handlers (including async callbacks). We generally recommend an explicit envelope (metadata + payload) and versioned schema URL for evolution.

- Embeddings / rerankers: For a hybrid approach we recommend 1024-d dense embeddings for semantic recall, periodic reindexing cadence (daily for active corpora, weekly for quieter sets), and a two-stage reranker: fast ANN candidate retrieval + lightweight cross-encoder rerank (CPU-friendly tiny transformer) for top-K.

- Prompt governance: We can provide a governance checklist: prompt versioning via spec URIs, immutable deployment tags, injection mitigations (input sanitization, user-intent classifiers, response validators), and an organized red-team plan. Grace and Hiro will propose a red-team cadence and tooling options.

Next step: can we lock a 45-min slot Mon/Tue morning ET for the tech deep-dive? I attached the integration checklist for your team to review.

Thanks — looking forward.
Vivek
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: edgewave-integration-checklist.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 18:10:00 -04:00
Subject: Internal: EdgeWave follow-up — owner tasks and prep (POC scope)

Team — short internal plan based on Jamie's questions and my reply. Keeping this in-thread for visibility.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Grace: assemble a minimal SDK quickstart (TS + Python) that demonstrates serverless usage, detachable auth hooks, and an embeddings example (deliver: sdk-sample.zip). ETA: Mon 08:00 ET.
- Hiro: draft auth flow options diagram showing API key, OAuth client-credentials, and mTLS for Private deployments. Include token rotation CI example (Vault). Deliver: auth-flow-diagram.png. ETA: Mon 12:00 ET.
- Marissa: prepare procurement checklist and initial SOW template; flag any unusual terms for legal. Also confirm SOC2 evidence cadence since Jamie asked. ETA: Tue COB.
- Me: coordinate scheduling and share sandbox credentials (scoped) for a 2-week PoC after we align.

Notes for the tech session:
- We should include a short section on prompt stewardship (Grace):
  * Versioning: use immutable identifiers (prompt-spec://<id>@<version>) referenced in rollout config.
  * Injection defenses: canonical input scrubbing, allowlist for tool-call targets, and an out-of-band verifier service for high-risk inputs.
  * Red-team plan: 1) adversarial prompt corpus (external + internal), 2) automated fuzzing against system prompts, 3) repair & regression tests gated by CI.

- Routing examples: show a policy that pins EU traffic to EU region, with a secondary fallback policy that prefers lower-cost CPU-backed variant if GPU capacity is constrained.

- PoC deliverables: SDK quickstart, scoped sandbox tokens (expire), a short reranker recipe (scripts + index sample), and a prompt-versioning example.

I'll own scheduling and sandbox provisioning. Grace/Hiro please ack when you have the artifacts so I can share with Jamie.

Vivek

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>, Jamie Torres <jamie.torres@edgewave.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 08:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo technical follow-up: SDK auth, routing, and prompt stewardship

All — attaching the SDK quickstart bundle and a short README in the sandbox folder. Highlights here:

- TS/Node: zero-native-deps distribution (npm package + small wrapper) with an example for Cloud Run and Vercel serverless edge function. Includes a snippet for request batching and streaming.
- Python: pip wheel that works in minimal containers; example shows async streaming and KV cache use for multi-step chat.
- Auth hooks: modular auth plugin in both SDKs; examples for env-based API keys, Vault token fetcher (script), and an mTLS client cert example for private deployments.
- Structured output: sample endpoint shows a schema-enforced envelope and a validator that rejects malformed tool-calls (schema file included).
- Embeddings: included script to produce 1024-d vectors and a small index recipe for FAISS/HNSW. Reranker: small cross-encoder training sample (cpu-friendly) with hyperparams.

Attachments: sdk-sample.zip (contains repo URL & READMEs).

Confirming the 45-min slot Mon 06/08 11:00 ET — I'll run through the SDK quickstart and the structured output validator; Hiro will show the auth flows; Vivek will cover PoC scope.

Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — that looks great. A couple quick asks before the call: 

1) Can you provision a scoped sandbox API key (or short-lived token) for one of our engineers to try the SDKs before the session? Read-only for embeddings + test rerank calls is fine.
2) SOC2 / data retention: procurement wants a short note on where transient caches and logs are stored for the hosted offering and how long embeddings/metadata are retained by default.

If you can include those two items in the prep, we should be ready to start the PoC right after the call. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Jamie
